subject: Dedicated capacity scope, technical asks, and ops playbook
messages:
From: Emily Chu <emily.chu@somatherapeutics.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + quick context for Fri call

Michael —

Thanks again for finding time this week. To give you some context before Friday: Soma Therapeutics is piloting LLM-driven triage for our internal research notes and molecular screening logs. Two hard constraints for us are isolation (data residency + strict network controls) and predictable throughput for nightly batch inference windows.

Rough numbers: ~120M tokens/day today across a mix of short (<=128 tokens) and long (up to 2,048 tokens) requests, plus a diurnal spike where we need sustained 120 concurrent sessions for 30–45 minutes. We expect these to grow by ~3x if latency and cost look good.

Please bring any materials on reserved GPU sizing, isolation options (VPC + private plane), burst strategies, and an ops playbook for outages/failover. I attached our SOC2 requirements doc to the calendar invite — happy to answer questions on that.

Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Emily
Emily Chu
Head of ML Ops, Soma Therapeutics
emily.chu@somatherapeutics.com
+1 415 555 0123

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chu <emily.chu@somatherapeutics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick context for Fri call

Emily —

Great context, thanks. Recap from our call just now and concrete next steps below. Ben (senior solutions engineer) and Priya (customer success) looped in for sizing and onboarding ops.

Key pain points we captured
- Isolation: "air-gapped"-style network controls, customer-managed VPC, KMS/HSM for keys, and strict egress rules.
- Predictable nightly throughput: need guaranteed capacity windows with low tail latency during the 30–45 minute spike.
- Cost sensitivity at scale: want clear levers (quantization, batching, cache) to manage per-token spend as usage grows.

Goals you stated
- Full isolation for all inference data and logs in your VPC.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for reserved pool; p95/p99 latency targets to be agreed in sizing.
- Initial reserved pool to cover current load with a 2x headroom for burst; plan for 3x growth in 12 months.

Technical notes & open questions (please confirm the numbered items)
1) Model family and size: you mentioned a mix of Llama-2-70B finetuned + a smaller 13B ensemble for short queries. Confirm model sizes and whether weights must remain private.
2) Typical sequence lengths: you listed 128 median, 2,048 max. Confirm 2,048 is rare (<=5% traffic).
3) Concurrency profile: sustained 120 sessions during nightly run for ~45 mins. Are these heavy KV-cache sessions (stateful) or stateless inference?
4) Tokenization: do you use batching-friendly tokenization (bpe/spm) or many short prompts with heavy system context?
5) Audit & logs: required retention window for request/response logs and for KV cache traces.

Proposed technical solution (high-level)
- Reserved GPU pool sized to cover 2x current baseline and handle the 120-concurrency window using a mix of A100x4-like instances and burstable GPUs for transient load.
- Private control plane + VPC peering for isolated networking; option for on-prem connector if you require air-gapped operations.
- KV cache with customer-side encryption and 30-day default retention (adjustable).
- Canary canary run for 2 weeks, then flip to reserved pool with rollback path to hosted variant.

Attached: draft capacity scope & ops playbook (RIF_dedicated_scope_v1.pdf).

Next steps & owners
- Emily: confirm model sizes, traffic split, and log retention requirement (items 1–4) — due Tue 6/16.
- Ben: will produce an initial sizing worksheet and latency estimates by Wed 6/17.
- Priya: will prepare an onboarding timeline and escalation runbook draft by Fri 6/19.
- Michael: will send an initial commercial outline and draft MAP (mutual action plan) link.

If this matches your expectations, I will convert the worksheet to a HubSpot proposal and share the Drive MAP.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0199

From: Julian Park <julian.park@somatherapeutics.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Emily Chu <emily.chu@somatherapeutics.com>
Cc: procurement@somatherapeutics.com
Date: 2026-06-12T14:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick context for Fri call

Thanks, Michael — that's a very clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Model weights will remain private; we need assurance they never leave our VPC or encrypted object store.
- 2,048 sequences are ~3% of traffic, usually for longer retrospective summaries.
- The nightly 120 concurrent window is stateful (threads where KV cache matters).
- Log retention: legal requires 90 days for request metadata; payload-level retention negotiable but default should be 30 days.

Procurement side: we prefer a 12-month reserved commitment with monthly usage reconciliation and the option to increase commit mid-term. We'll share a boilerplate SOW and PO process.

I'll ask procurement to send the boilerplate SOW to Michael and Priya.

-Julian
Julian Park
CTO, Soma Therapeutics
julian.park@somatherapeutics.com

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Julian Park <julian.park@somatherapeutics.com>, Emily Chu <emily.chu@somatherapeutics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick context for Fri call

Appreciate the clarifications, Julian — that helps a lot. Updated actions and timeline below (short and actionable):

Confirmed technical constraints
- Model weights: remain private; we will design a deploy variant that keeps weights in your S3/KMS boundary and uses only inference binaries in the dedicated pool.
- Sequence distribution: 3% long sequences, 97% <= 512 tokens for planning purposes.
- Stateful nightly window: treat as sticky sessions with KV-cache affinity; will size accordingly.
- Log retention: baseline 90-day request metadata retention; payload retention default 30 days unless compliance prefers otherwise.

Immediate next actions (owners & dates)
- Emily: share the model artifact storage pattern and a sample anonymized token distribution CSV — due 2026-06-16.
- Ben: deliver sizing worksheet + latency SLOs (p95/p99 estimates) — due 2026-06-17. Ben will include both steady-state and burst sizing and a recommended reserved commit.
- Priya: draft onboarding runbook + procurement handoff checklist (includes PO/SOW steps) — due 2026-06-19.
- Michael: prepare commercial sketch (term options, commit tiers, break/fallback policies) and publish the MAP in Drive — due 2026-06-18. HubSpot deal created: https://hubspot.example/deal/SOMA-2026-022

Scheduling: propose a technical deep-dive (Ben + Priya + our infra lead) on Tue 2026-06-23 10:00–11:00 PT. Let me know if that works and I will send a calendar invite.

Risks called out now
- If KV cache is stateful and owned by the customer, cross-GPU affinity constraints may increase reserved footprint; we'll quantify in the worksheet.
- SOC2 evidence: we'll provide controls mapping and can run a joint readiness call with our security team.

Attachments & links
- Draft capacity scope (RIF_dedicated_scope_v1.pdf) — see attached.
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MAP-Redwood-Soma-MAP
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/SOMA-2026-022

If that looks good I'll convert the worksheet into a proposal and share a draft SOW template for procurement to review.

Thanks —
Michael
